---
title: "About this prototype"
subtitle: "Purpose, scope and a practical first phase"
---

Prepared by **Lilly Jones, PhD**, as a discussion prototype following interest in adapting the Tribal Fire Science sandbox for ESIIL. This release is not an official ESIIL product or an agreement with any named Nation or organization.                                        

## What is ready

- Four executable research notebooks and a readable companion site.
- Real MTBS context examples for four regional windows.
- Six distinct public-source case contexts, including separate Southern Ute and Ute Mountain Ute discussions and separate Yurok and Karuk cases.
- Blank research, governance, exchange and monitoring materials.
- Validated paired-analysis code that requires observations before estimating outcomes.

## A proposed first phase

| Step | Proposed work | What completion would look like |
|---|---|---|
| Frame | Discuss the four modules with Jennifer and relevant ESIIL colleagues | A narrower question, intended audience and suitable existing program connection |
| Invite | Ask appropriate existing and prospective partners whether the work would be useful | Willing participation and clearly identified authorities; no inferred agreement |
| Design | Agree on benefits, compensation, data handling and interpretation | A completed partner brief and monitoring protocol where wanted |
| Pilot | Use one public-data teaching example and, if agreed, one partner-defined study | A useful learning output and documented feedback |
| Review | Decide what to revise, share or discontinue | Partner-specific release decisions and an agreed next step |

## What stays outside this first release

Active-fire prediction, burn prescriptions, automated “opportunity” or capacity rankings, cultural-site mapping and unvalidated fire-speed experiments. Weather, smoke, watershed and advanced modeling modules can be considered after the core questions and relationships are clearer.

## Lineage and licensing

The starting point was the Tribal Fire Science sandbox by Lilly Jones, developed in consultation with James Sanovia. The new project retains that lineage and the AGPL-3.0 license, while using a smaller, newly written analysis package. The existing sandbox was left untouched. [Original software citation](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19265139).

Third-party source materials retain their own terms. The software license does not confer rights over Indigenous knowledge, partner observations or third-party content.
